title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles failed during a foreseeable high-traffic event when their batteries drained during extended periods of congestion on San Francisco streets. The system was deployed into conditions it was not built to handle: major traffic disruptions, high traveler volumes, and unplanned road closures following Fourth of July celebrations. A vehicle also caught fire after driving over fireworks debris, suggesting the system lacks adequate detection or avoidance of hazards in chaotic urban environments.

This is a deployment failure in real-world traffic management rather than a model error. The vehicles became stationary and required towing, creating additional congestion for human drivers. Better battery capacity for extended idle periods, improved prediction of traffic disruption events, or human intervention protocols before vehicle incapacity could have prevented the stranding.

It is not established whether the battery drain was caused by the vehicles making inefficient routing decisions, attempting maneuvers that consumed excess power, or simply sitting in traffic with climate control and systems running. It is also not established what safeguards existed to alert operators before battery levels became critical.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets on Saturday during heavy Fourth of July traffic following fireworks celebrations near the Golden Gate Bridge. Videos verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up stationary on streets, with some requiring towing after their batteries drained during the congestion. The company cited major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures as contributing factors. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported. Frustrated motorists spent extended periods stuck behind the driverless cars, with one driver reporting nearly two hours of standstill traffic.

Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to strengthen resilience during major traffic disruptions. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to have conversations with public and private partners about improving the experience for future events. This incident follows a previous December outage when Waymo vehicles stalled at intersections with nonworking traffic lights. The city's Department of Emergency Management had warned residents about heavy post-fireworks traffic before the event occurred.
